controls.title: Business impact analysis
controls.summary: The vendor has performed a documented business impact analysis identifying maximum tolerable downtime for services it provides.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for service-specific RTO/RPO figures, not a generic statement of commitment to continuity.

controls.title: Business continuity strategy
controls.summary: A documented strategy exists for maintaining or recovering critical services within the identified tolerable downtime.
controls.validationGuidance: Strategy should be specific to the services delivered to this customer segment, not enterprise-wide only.

controls.title: Tested recovery procedures
controls.summary: Recovery procedures have been tested within the last 12 months with documented results.
controls.validationGuidance: A written plan without evidence of an actual test or exercise should be treated as a gap, not a pass.

controls.title: Alternate processing and data center arrangements
controls.summary: Geographically separated failover infrastructure exists for services supporting critical customer functions.
controls.validationGuidance: Verify actual geographic separation, not two availability zones in the same metro region for a genuinely critical vendor.

controls.title: Supply chain continuity dependencies
controls.summary: The continuity plan accounts for the vendor's own critical suppliers, not only its internal infrastructure.
controls.validationGuidance: Direct overlap with NIST 800-161 C-SCRM-9 - a shared evidence excerpt can typically satisfy both.

controls.title: Crisis communication plan
controls.summary: A defined communication plan specifies how affected customers are notified during a disruption, including timelines.
controls.validationGuidance: Check for a specific notification SLA, matching the pattern flagged as commonly missing in FFIEC-6 and GLBA-9.

controls.title: Exercise and continual improvement program
controls.summary: A recurring exercise program (tabletop or live failover) drives continual improvement of the continuity plan.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence of lessons-learned being incorporated into a revised plan, not just repeated identical exercises.

controls.title: Management review and resourcing
controls.summary: Senior management reviews the continuity program and allocates resources sufficient to maintain it.
controls.validationGuidance: Typically the weakest-evidenced control for smaller vendors - a dated management review record is strong evidence when present.
